To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity of the RNA polymerase in the nuclei of the livers of normal intact mice is increased after gamma-irradiation, whereas the RNA polymerase activity in the nuclei of liver cells of adrenalectomised mice remains unchanged.

1) the RNA polymerase activity in nuclei of liver cells of intact γ-irradiation mice increases, 2) this increase is absent in adrenalectomised animals, and 3) the RNA polymerases in the nuclei of the liver cells of intact mice are of a high molecular weight, whereas the polymerases in the cells of adrenalectomied animals are of a low molecular weight.
the transcription of RNA in the liver of mice increases significantly after gamma irradiation, and that this effect is not observed in mice whose adrenal glands were previously removed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the study of RNA polymerase activity in the liver nuclei of intact or adrenalectomised mice after whole body γ-irradiation.
the effect of gamma-irradiation on the RNA polymerase activity of the mouse liver nuclei.
the effects of gamma irradiation on the activity of the DNA dependent RNA polymerase in the liver nuclei of mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RNA polymerase activity of liver nuclei of γ-irradiate mice increases significantly and that this increase is not observed in adrenalectomised mice.
the effect of adrenalectomy in vivo and of corticoid administration in vitro is to inhibit transcription of the DNA of the liver cell nucleus by RNA polymerase.
the RNA polymerase activity in mouse liver is increased by γ-irradiation and this is mediated through the adrenal glands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transcription of the genes encoding the ribosomal RNAs in liver nuclei of mice is stimulated by the γ-irradiation of the intact animal, and that this stimulation is abolished in the absence of the adrenals.

we found a significant increase in the RNA polymerase activity in the liver nuclei of intact mice, following γ-irradiation of the whole animal, while no such increase was observed in the adrenalectomised mice.
we have shown that the transcription of the rDNA in the nucleolar organizing region of mouse cells can be regulated by the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA polymerases are sensitive to radiation, and this sensitivity is dependent on the cell cycle phase.
we have shown that the transcription of the gene for the 60S ribosomal subunit is regulated by a feedback mechanism.
the RNA polymerase II CTD has an intrinsic ability to bind and regulate the function of the transcriptional machinery.
